data.exact_reserve_text: 2017 and prior year: The 2017 and prior year has been closed with a loss of GBP 52.0m (52.0% loss on capacity). The key components of the movement in the spot result over 2019 are set out below:
data.standardized_narrative: The gross claims reserves opened at GBP 128.664m. Analysis of the development triangle indicates a small net prior-year strengthening of approximately GBP 0.58m (c.0.45% of opening reserves), driven by movement in older underwriting years (notably 2015) while 2016 and 2017 were broadly stable. The managing agent highlights adverse large-loss experience in Energy and Political Risk / D&O classes and notes RITC and run-off related costs affecting results, but no specific named catastrophe events are quantified in the prior-year movement.
raw_causal_phrases: Higher than previously reserved premium receipts, primarily arising from the cargo, hull and political risk classes
Negative specific large loss experience arising from new losses on the political risk, D&O and energy classes
Stable experience in attritional and catastrophe reserves across all other classes of business

Additional Run-off & RITC costs include the net impact of risk premium paid to the 2018 YOA, provision for 2020 run-off costs allocated to 2017 and prior YOA business, and favourable movement in 2016 & prior reserves
The 2017 and prior year has been closed with a loss of GBP 52.0m (52.0% loss on capacity)

gross_premium_mix.line_of_business: Fire and other damage to property

data.data_quality_notes: Prior-year development derived from the gross claims development table (triangle). The syndicate completed RITC/closure activity (2017 & prior closed into 2018) which can distort year comparisons; narrative references describe adverse large losses in Energy/Political/D&O but do not quantify gross PYD. The triangle values are presented in GBP 000 (thousands) and the prior-year development result is small relative to total reserves; confidence reduced to 0.8 for PYD because of potential RITC/run-off allocations and the aggregation of 'prior' years in some narrative lines.
